demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. Calls from the shell impersonate documind-ui-sa, the UI's own account, which make roster put on the three golden tenants (acme, zeta, globex). That is why a shell call can name any of the three. otok mints a token for documind-outsider-sa, an account IAM admits into the service and no roster lists. Tokens last about an hour; the functions mint a fresh one on every call. Your browser session is different: IAP signs you in as yourself, and the roster maps your email to exactly one tenant. Keep the two apart in your head; step 3 makes the difference visible. The stage's two settings and the retrieval backend live in the API's environment. A name the service does not set is unset here rather than exported empty, because the kit's settings class reads an empty variable as a value, and an empty QUERY_REWRITE is a value the validator refuses. svc_env is the helper lessons 2.2 to 2.4 define; step 6 reads the template with it again. Step 7's ablation reranks through the Ranking API's client at the API's own pin; the pip line is harmless if it is already there.

demos.heading: The stage in the kit: the call, the guard, one line in /v1/query, and two lines that did not change
demos.purpose: The cell asks the kit's guard about one question and five rewrites of it: a faithful one, the same one spelt with an en dash, the rupee sign and Devanagari digits, the amount written without its comma, the unit given another word, and the section spelt out. Nothing leaves the machine. evals/tests/test_query_rewrite.py holds 20 tests that need neither a model nor a lane: the guard on the design's examples and on the golden rows, every outcome against a fake client, the request against google-genai's own config class, the line with no question text, search_query() lifted from rewrite.py with the switch off and on, and the ablation's rewrite arm and paraphrase rows against a stand-in lane. The pipe keeps the summary and drops the timing.

demos.heading: The stage on a candidate: QUERY_REWRITE=on, a forced failure, and the undo
demos.purpose: The cell creates the revision and asks it the paraphrase from step 3. ask() prints the stage's three keys, the clocks, the answer's cost and the citations. If the first line says same, the model judged the question a good search query already; ask another of step 5's questions, such as pp-10's, the same way. QUERY_REWRITE_MODEL is a setting, so a revision whose model name is wrong is one variable away. The call fails, rewrite() catches it, and the stage searches the question: the answer still comes, with HTTP 200. Do it: the two lines the two questions wrote The variables exist only on the candidate's template, so they are removed rather than set back, and the tag is dropped. steps.label: bash — run in the operator shell, in $DEMO_ROOT (a Python cell; edits one kit file in your clone, never the lane)
steps.expected:
5 rules left; the prompt version still says 2026-10-08.1
- Use the words those documents use: the formal term for an informal one, and the full name of a law or a term beside its abbreviation.
- Keep every condition the question sets: who is asking, which document, before or after, the least or the most.
- Do not answer the question, and add no fact, figure or name that is not in it.
- The question may be in English, in Hindi written in Devanagari, or in Hinglish (Hindi typed in Latin letters); write the query in English.
- One line of at most 40 words. If the question is already a good search query, return it unchanged.
